Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks for the quick review of the order form. Attached is Nimbus_OrderForm_v3.pdf with our commercial redlines (pricing table + min-commit phasing). A couple of open points we want to resolve before we send the DocuSign package: 

1) Invoice waterfall: Acme requested entity-level invoicing. Our commercial ops team is proposing a primary-invoice + mirror credit flow (primary Redwood invoice to Acme US entity, secondary settlement to local entity via crediting) to avoid multi-entity VAT headaches. I attached a short proposal spreadsheet we can iterate on.

2) Minimum commit phasing: the customer prefers a front-loaded min commit but wants the invoice timing to match quarterly usage milestones. We need to agree whether min-commit invoices will be charged up front or amortized over the first two quarters. Pricing impact is small but affects finance recognition.

3) Tax residency / withholding: please confirm the form of tax residency evidence you can provide (certificate of residence, W-8BEN-E, local equivalents). We have to ensure no withholding is applied in the EU scenario.

Could you confirm: (A) if Acme can accept the primary-invoice / crediting waterfall (file: InvoiceWaterfall_proposal.xlsx), and (B) what tax evidence you can provide? If both are OK we'll ask legal to finalize the two redline bullets in the MSA appendix and prepare the DocuSign order form.

Attachments: Nimbus_OrderForm_v3.pdf (order form w/ redlines)

Next step: Laura — if you can confirm by Monday we can circulate the final DocuSign.

Thanks Laura — 

I pulled finance and legal into a quick alignment. High level proposal from our side: 
- Invoice waterfall: Redwood will issue a primary invoice to the Acme US entity (per our billing system) that nets to the aggregate min commit. We will then issue entity-level credit memos to reflect the allocation to local entities; credits will be processed within 30 days of the primary invoice. This keeps recognition consistent on our side and gives Acme entity-level accounting artifacts. See attached InvoiceWaterfall_proposal.xlsx for the mapping.
- Net terms: we can accommodate Net 60 on the primary invoice tied to min commit but need a short payment schedule appendix in the order form clarifying due dates for following invoices.
- Tax / withholding: we will accept a tax residency certificate. To avoid grossing-up, we propose a clause where each party retains responsibility for its own withholding and Redwood will provide VAT evidence for any credits issued back to local entities. We'll add a sentence to the MSA appendix to that effect.

Action items for Redwood legal:
1) Add a one-line payment appendix describing Net 60 for the primary invoice and credit timing.
2) Add a tax-evidence clause and a VAT credit/offset mechanism.

I've attached our spreadsheet and a sample redline comment for legal. If Acme confirms Net 60 + tax evidence, Rishi can move this to DocuSign.

Attachment: InvoiceWaterfall_proposal.xlsx

Laura / team —

Quick commercial note from pricing: amortizing the min commit over the first two quarters vs charging up front changes recognition but only shifts ~3% of ARR timing for this deal. If we amortize, we need to lock in the per-token price for the first two quarters (no mid-quarter repricing). If billed up front, the customer gets the flexibility to apply credits later but Redwood takes earlier revenue recognition.

On VAT/withholding: add a simple clause that Redwood will provide VAT evidence for credits within 45 days and Acme agrees to notify Redwood of any local withholding at invoice receipt. That should prevent surprise deductions.
